integration_questions: With wheel_track at 0.16 m, does the robot still turn sharply enough on the slalom, or does line loss rise at the tightest bends compared with 0.14 m?
Does the wider track allow a higher kp or kd without oscillation on the oval, and which gain range was stable?
Does max_error still peak at the same point on the s-bend, and does line loss occur at that point?
Are the outer sensors (x = +/-0.06 m) carrying much signal, and could they be given smaller weights to reduce line loss on the slalom?
feedback_request.requested_format: Brief notes on each question, plus the single geometry change you would make first if you could change only one thing.

intent: Continue the single-variable wheel-track sweep from iteration 4 by moving wheel_track from 0.14 to 0.16 m, keeping the seven-sensor, 0.12 m span, 16 mm footprint, y = 0.06 m, 0.6 kg layout that gave the best score. I expect a further gain on the s-bend and oval from reduced bend overshoot, and a score at or above 517. If the score falls, the optimum lies near 0.14 m and the next lever is sensing (span or footprint) rather than track width.
learning: Track width has a monotonic effect on this family: 0.10 m (357) < 0.12 m (483) < 0.14 m (517). Hypotheses to test: (1) 0.16 m continues the trend and raises s-bend finishes; (2) the trend flattens or reverses by 0.16 m, because the slalom's sharpest bends need more turn authority than the wider track gives; (3) the slalom stays at 0 finishes whatever the track, so it needs a sensing change (span or footprint) next. Measurements to request on each development track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort.
rationale: Race evidence: iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.14 m, other geometry as iteration 1) is the best design so far at 517.07. Across the three clean wheel-track points, the score rises monotonically with track width: 0.10 m gave 357.3 (iteration 3), 0.12 m gave 482.7 (iteration 1) and 0.14 m gave 517.1 (iteration 4). Holding every other variable fixed, the narrow track made the robot overshoot bends, with oval finishes falling from 20/20 to 14/20 and s-bend finishes from 5/20 to 1/20. The wider track damped that overshoot: s-bend finishes rose to 6/20 and the s-bend mean score rose to 519. Every failure is still an off-track end with max_error at or above 0.06 m, while rms_error stays at 0.026 to 0.031 m, so the limit is occasional large excursions, not steady tracking. The slalom has never finished (0/20 in every iteration), with about 0.9 to 1.0 line-loss events per run and progress near 0.2. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit, since max(0.06, 0.0125 + width/4) stays at 0.06 m across the allowed range. I will keep the iteration 4 layout and change only wheel_track, from 0.14 to 0.16 m, to test whether the monotonic trend continues. Sensor span, footprint, lead, mass, wheel radius and body stay fixed so the change is attributable. Expected result: fewer bend excursions on the s-bend, more s-bend finishes, and a score at or above 517. Main risk: at 0.16 m the robot may turn too slowly for the slalom's tightest bends, which would raise line-loss events there and could lower the oval score.
